mcqs.q: All lining mucosa shares which feature?
mcqs.explain: Lining mucosa is non-keratinized; it is subdivided into loosely attached (movable) and firmly attached types.

mcqs.q: Which is LOOSELY attached (movable) lining mucosa?
opts: Alveolar mucosa, vestibular fornix and floor of mouth
mcqs.explain: Loosely attached lining mucosa includes the alveolar mucosa, vestibular fornix and floor of mouth; lip, cheek, ventral tongue and soft palate are firmly attached.

mcqs.q: The epithelium of the alveolar mucosa is:
opts: Thin and non-keratinized, with few or missing rete pegs
Thick and keratinized with tall rete pegs
mcqs.explain: Alveolar mucosa has a thin, non-keratinized epithelium with few or missing rete pegs.

mcqs.q: A prominent feature of the lamina propria and submucosa of alveolar mucosa is:
opts: Many elastic fibres (allowing mobility) and extensive vasculature
mcqs.explain: Alveolar mucosa has many elastic fibres and an extensive vascular supply, with minor mixed salivary glands in the submucosa; it is loosely attached to the alveolar process.

mcqs.q: The alveolar mucosa meets the attached gingiva at the:
mcqs.explain: The mucogingival junction marks the boundary between the loose alveolar mucosa and the firm attached gingiva.

mcqs.q: In the floor of the mouth, the small papilla beside the lingual frenum that carries the submandibular duct opening is the:
mcqs.explain: The sublingual caruncle, on each side of the lingual frenum, carries the opening of the submandibular gland duct.

mcqs.q: The rounded ridge extending back and laterally from the sublingual caruncle, produced by the sublingual gland, is the:
mcqs.explain: The sublingual fold is a rounded ridge produced by the sublingual gland and contains its ducts.

mcqs.q: The epithelium of the floor of the mouth is:
mcqs.explain: The floor of the mouth has a very thin, non-keratinized epithelium with a highly vascular lamina propria — ideal for rapid (sublingual) absorption.

mcqs.q: The buccal and labial mucosa epithelium is:
mcqs.explain: Buccal/labial mucosa has a thick, non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with irregular blunt CT papillae; it is firmly attached to the underlying muscle.

mcqs.q: Stensen's (parotid) duct opens into the buccal mucosa at the parotid papilla, opposite the:
mcqs.explain: Stensen's (parotid) duct opens at the parotid papilla in the buccal mucosa, opposite the second maxillary molar.

mcqs.q: Elastic fibres in the lamina propria of the buccal mucosa serve to:
mcqs.explain: Elastic fibres in the lamina propria prevent folding of the buccal mucosa; minor mixed salivary glands provide lubrication.

mcqs.q: The ventral (inferior) surface of the tongue shows which characteristic histologic feature?
opts: A 'saw-tooth' appearance of the epithelial ridges
mcqs.explain: The ventral tongue has thin non-keratinized epithelium with a saw-tooth ridge pattern (numerous short CT papillae) and no distinct submucosa — it merges with the muscle.

mcqs.q: The ventral surface of the tongue has:
opts: No distinct submucosa (it merges with the muscle)
mcqs.explain: On the ventral tongue there is no distinct submucosa; the lamina propria merges with the muscle fibres, and it is firmly attached.

mcqs.q: Compared with the hard palate, the soft palate:
opts: Has no bony framework and is non-keratinized
mcqs.explain: The soft palate has no bony framework; its epithelium is thin and non-keratinized, with a distinct elastic layer in the lamina propria.

mcqs.q: A distinctive feature of the soft palate's lamina propria is:
opts: A distinct elastic layer, and it is highly vascular
mcqs.explain: The soft palate lamina propria is thick with numerous CT papillae and a distinct elastic layer, and is highly vascular; it is firmly attached to muscle.

mcqs.q: Which structure forms the midline attachment in the floor of the mouth, allowing the anterior tongue to move?
mcqs.explain: The lingual frenum is a midline mucosal fold connecting the tongue to the floor of the mouth, allowing the anterior part to move.

mcqs.q: Which lining mucosa is firmly (not loosely) attached?
mcqs.explain: The cheek, lip, ventral tongue and soft palate are firmly attached lining mucosa; alveolar mucosa, vestibular fornix and floor of mouth are loosely attached.

mcqs.q: Why is the alveolar mucosa redder than the attached gingiva?
opts: Thin non-keratinized epithelium over an extensive vascular supply
mcqs.explain: The alveolar mucosa's thin, non-keratinized epithelium over a highly vascular lamina propria makes it appear redder than the firm, paler gingiva.

mcqs.q: Minor salivary glands in the lining mucosa are located in the:
mcqs.explain: Minor (mixed) salivary glands lie in the submucosa of lining mucosa (alveolar, buccal, labial, floor, soft palate), providing lubrication.

mcqs.q: The floor of the mouth is supported by which muscles?
mcqs.explain: The floor of the mouth is formed by the mylohyoid and geniohyoid muscles, covered with mucous membrane.

mcqs.q: Which feature best identifies the soft palate vs other lining mucosa on a slide?
opts: A distinct elastic layer in a thick, highly vascular lamina propria
mcqs.explain: The soft palate is identified by its thick, highly vascular lamina propria with a distinct elastic layer.

mcqs.q: The CT papillae of the alveolar mucosa are:
mcqs.explain: In alveolar mucosa the connective-tissue papillae are sometimes missing or poorly developed, contributing to its smooth surface.

saqs.q: Subdivide lining mucosa by attachment, giving examples.
saqs.a: Loosely attached (movable): alveolar mucosa, vestibular fornix, floor of mouth. Firmly attached: lip, cheek, ventral tongue, soft palate.

saqs.q: Describe the histology of the alveolar mucosa.
saqs.a: Thin non-keratinized epithelium (few rete pegs), lamina propria with many elastic fibres and rich vasculature, submucosa with minor glands; loosely attached at the mucogingival junction.
Lingual frenum (midline), sublingual caruncle (submandibular duct opening), and sublingual fold (sublingual gland).

saqs.q: Describe the histology of the buccal/labial mucosa.
saqs.a: Thick non-keratinized epithelium; lamina propria with irregular blunt papillae, elastic fibres and extensive vasculature; submucosa with fat and minor glands; firmly attached to muscle.

saqs.q: What is distinctive about the ventral tongue mucosa?
saqs.a: Thin non-keratinized epithelium with a saw-tooth ridge pattern and no distinct submucosa (merges with muscle); firmly attached.

saqs.q: Describe the histology of the soft palate.
saqs.a: Thin non-keratinized epithelium; thick, highly vascular lamina propria with a distinct elastic layer; thin submucosa with glands; no bony framework, firmly attached to muscle.

saqs.q: Where does Stensen's duct open and at what level?
saqs.a: Into the buccal mucosa at the parotid papilla, opposite the second maxillary molar.
